why: B as written is false: it allows n = 0, where its first conjunct says S(X₀,X₀) ≤ 0 (empty sum) for every subadditive S, refuted by S ≡ 1 (not_B). So A ⇒ B is false and B ⇒ A holds only vacuously. The project's lemmas assume 0 < n. With that hypothesis added (Bpos), the two are equivalent, and both directions are proved. A ⇒ Bpos: apply le_sum_of_chain to S' a b = S b a; the additive case uses it for S and for -S. Bpos ⇒ A: encode a chain as the sets Iic i ⊆ ℕ. For le_sum_of_chain, whose hypothesis (subadditivity only on X₀ ⊆ X_m ⊆ X_{m+1}) is weaker, the missing values are set to S(X₀,X_c) - S(X₀,X_a) so that subadditivity holds on the whole chain. relation 'equivalent' refers to A vs the corrected Bpos.
B_issue: B includes the case n = 0, where S(X₀,X₀) ≤ 0 is not implied by subadditivity (which only gives S(X,X) ≥ 0); Milnor's chain implicitly has n ≥ 1. With 0 < n added, B is correct.
